title: Working at Redwood: Comprehensive Handbook — Roles, Careers, Benefits, Hiring, Onboarding & Tools
author: Ava Morgan
content:
Purpose

This document is the canonical Redwood employee handbook summary for 'Working at Redwood'. It consolidates our values and expectations, role and career ladder guidance, benefits and perks information, a high-level hiring and onboarding overview, and day-1/day-30/day-90 quickstarts for the most-used internal tools. The intended audience is new hires, hiring managers, and people-ops partners.

Summary / Table of contents
1) Working at Redwood: values, expectations, and work model
2) Roles & career ladders: leveled frameworks, promotion process, and resources
3) Benefits & perks: enrollment, common questions, and owner contacts
4) Hiring & onboarding overview: candidate lifecycle and new hire milestones
5) Internal tools guide: access checklist and team quickstarts
6) Contacts, ownership, and update cadence

1) Working at Redwood: values, expectations, and work model
Core values (short)
- Customer-first: ship with measurable customer value and iterate based on feedback.
- Pragmatic excellence: production readiness, observability, and cost-awareness are engineering priorities.
- Psychological safety: promote inclusive debate and constructive feedback.
- Ownership: take end-to-end responsibility for services and deliverables.

Behavioral expectations
- Communicate status and risks proactively in team channels and weekly syncs.
- Use data and evidence when making product or technical trade-offs.
- Follow code of conduct, security policies, and legal guidelines documented under Security & Compliance.

Work model and time off
- Hybrid-first: teams decide office cadence; expect at least one in-person team event or all-hands quarterly.
- Flexible remote options available with manager approval for role-specific requirements.
- PTO: unlimited policy; recommended minimum 15 days/year. Request time off through HR Portal.
- Holidays: company-observed holidays listed annually in HR Portal.

2) Roles & career ladders: leveled frameworks, promotion process, and resources
Leveled frameworks (overview)
- Engineering (E1-1E5): E1 Associate through E5 Principal. Each level includes examples of scope, autonomy, and expected impact.
- Product (P1-1P5): Associate PM through Director/Head, with emphasis on roadmap ownership and cross-functional execution.
- Design, Solutions, CS, and Sales: parallel leveled frameworks documented in their respective team pages.

Promotion process (high level)
1) Candidate assembles packet: impact write-ups, metrics, examples, and peer feedback.
2) Manager endorsement: manager reviews packet and recommends promotion.
3) Promotion Committee review: committee evaluates against rubric and confirms decision within ~6 weeks.
4) Communication and calibration: feedback shared with candidate and next steps agreed.

Promotion evaluation themes
- Scope & impact: measurable outcomes and breadth of ownership.
- Craft & skill: technical or role-specific proficiency.
- Influence & leadership: cross-team impact and mentorship.
- Consistent execution: reliability and quality over time.

Resources and templates
- Promotion packet template: people-ops/promotion-template (Confluence).
- Role rubrics and leveling criteria: people-ops/role-rubrics.

3) Benefits & perks: enrollment, common questions, and owner contacts
Health & wellbeing
- Medical, dental, and vision: multiple plans with company contribution. New hires must enroll within 30 days of start date via HR Portal.
- EAP and mental health subsidy: confidential counseling and therapy stipend available.

Compensation & equity
- Base salary and annual bonus targets by level; equity grant on hire and refresh awards annually. Compensation decisions coordinated with Finance.

Family & time away
- Parental leave: primary caregiver 18 weeks paid; secondary caregiver 8 weeks paid. Additional unpaid leave options exist and are handled case-by-case.

Learning & development
- Annual learning stipend: $2,000 per employee (pro-rated first year). Request reimbursements via People Ops.
- Conference and training budget: team-managed with manager approval.

Work setup & equipment
- Onboarding equipment stipend: $1,500 one-time. Request via IT ticket.
- Remote work stipend: $100/month.

Perks & recognition
- Quarterly hackathons, team retreats, and recognition awards.
- Spot bonuses and peer-nominated awards administered by People Ops.

How to enroll and who to contact
- Use HR Portal (hr.redwood.ai) for plan selection, address updates, and dependent additions.
- People Ops benefits contact: benefits@redwood.ai

4) Hiring & onboarding overview: candidate lifecycle and new hire milestones
Hiring philosophy
We hire for ownership, operational thinking, and cross-functional collaboration. Interview loops emphasize production-oriented problem solving and communication.

Standard technical hiring flow
1) Recruiter screen (30-145m) to establish fit and logistics.
2) Technical screen (45-100m) focused on coding or system design by level.
3) Onsite/virtual loop (4-6 interviews) covering technical depth, design, product sense, and collaboration.
4) Debrief and calibration: feedback entered in Greenhouse; hiring manager compiles decision.
5) Offer, negotiation, and background checks.
6) Pre-boarding and Day 1 logistics: Welcome email with agenda, access, and initial reading.

Interviewer guidelines
- Use rubrics and provide specific, timely feedback (within 24 hours).
- Evaluate for production thinking, trade-off reasoning, and communication clarity.

Onboarding milestones
- Day 0 (pre-start): complete HR forms, set up direct deposit, and accept SSO invite.
- Day 1: People Ops welcome, manager 1:1 for 30/60/90 goals, and IT setup.
- Week 1: codebase walkthrough, security training completion, and small first task.
- 30/60/90 checkpoints: merge first PR, broader contributions, and final onboarding review with calibration.

5) Internal tools guide: access checklist and team quickstarts
Central quick links
- Slack: workspace.redwood.ai
- Confluence: confluence.redwood.ai
- HR Portal: hr.redwood.ai
- Identity & Access (SSO + MFA): idp.redwood.ai
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference
- Jira: jira.redwood.ai
- CI/CD: ci.redwood.ai
- Vault / Secrets: vault.redwood.ai
- VPN / Bastion: vpn.redwood.ai (request via Access form)

Day 0/1 access checklist
- Accept SSO invitation and enroll MFA.
- Request GitHub org membership and repo access via Access form.
- Join Slack workspace and team channels (#team-*, #announcements).
- Ensure laptop imaging and MDM enrollment are completed.
- Complete required security and compliance modules in Confluence.

Developer quickstart (high level)
- Clone key repos: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/<repo>.git
- Setup and run tests: make setup; make test
- PR expectations: clear description, testing instructions, and codeowner review. Follow PR template in GitHub.

Product & GTM quickstart
- Access PRD templates, roadmap boards, and customer playbooks in Confluence.
- Attend weekly product sync and onboarding sessions for Solutions and CS.

Security & secrets handling
- Never store secrets in repositories. Use vault.redwood.ai for secrets and KMS for key management.
- All production changes must include traceable approvals and audit logs. Refer to Security runbooks before deploying.

6) Contacts, ownership, and update cadence
Primary contacts
- People Ops (general): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Benefits: benefits@redwood.ai
- IT & access: it-support@redwood.ai
- Recruiting: recruiting@redwood.ai
- Security & compliance: security@redwood.ai

Document ownership and updates
- Primary owner: People Ops; secondary owner: Eng Developer Experience for tooling sections.
- Review cadence: quarterly review; emergency updates as required. To propose edits, create a Confluence edit request and notify people-ops@redwood.ai.

Appendix: useful templates and links
- Promotion packet template: people-ops/promotion-template
- Manager 30/60/90 checklist: people-ops/manager-checklist
- New hire welcome email template: recruiting/templates/welcome-email

End of document

Notes
- For team-specific exceptions (equipment beyond standard stipend, discretionary learning funds, or office budgets), coordinate with People Ops and obtain manager approval.
- For legal or compliance questions related to parental leave or international benefits, contact People Ops and Legal.
